metadata.description: Name of the azd environment (used as prefix for resources).
Azure region for all resources.
Region for the Foundry account+project. Leave empty to reuse location. Use a Voice Live supported region (eastus2, swedencentral, southeastasia, centralindia, westus2) if location is not one.
Name of the resource group to create / deploy into.
Object ID of the deploying principal (for direct role assignments, optional).
Name of an existing Application Insights component to reuse. Leave empty to create a new one in this RG.
Resource group of the existing Application Insights component. Defaults to the deployment RG when empty.
Foundry connection name for the Grounding-with-Bing-Custom-Search resource. Surfaces as BING_CONNECTION_NAME in the container.
Bing Custom Search configuration (instance) name — the curated domain allow-list. Surfaces as BING_CUSTOM_CONFIG_NAME in the container.

Deploy Grounding with Bing Custom Search: the Bing account, the curated site allow-list, and the Foundry connection. Opt-in and additive — when false nothing Bing-related is created and the agent runs on AI Search alone.

Voice Live binding.

"agent" (default) routes every turn through the Foundry agent: speech is
transcribed by a recognizer, the agent reasons and calls its managed AI Search
and Bing grounding tools, and the reply is synthesised back to speech.

"model" binds Voice Live straight to a realtime speech-to-speech model. The
recognizer stage disappears from the answer path, and the tools become
in-process Python functions instead of Foundry-managed ones.

Additive: leaving this unset gives exactly today's behaviour.
Realtime model to bind when voiceBinding is "model". Voice Live deploys and manages this model itself — no model deployment, no quota request. Ignored in agent mode.

"true"/"false" string. Developer mode exposes the settings panel, live transcript
and per-event logging, so settings can be changed and tried live while testing.
It changes no pipeline default: the panel is pre-populated with the same values
production uses.

Additive: leaving this unset gives exactly the production experience — panel
hidden, settings locked, session auto-starts.

It does not expose voiceBinding, which is deployment-wide by design.

Web IQ base URL. This is the web tool in model mode, where the agent (and therefore its managed Bing grounding tool) is out of the picture. Leave empty to use the code default — the tool is switched on by webIqApiKey, not by this.

Comma-separated hosts that scope Web IQ searches, e.g. "mtn.com,sashares.co.za". Web IQ has no server-side allow-list, so these are compiled into site: operators on the query. Same intent as bingAllowedDomains — an open-web tool answering to an executive should not be able to cite anywhere at all. Empty searches the open web.
Web IQ API key. Stored as a container-app secret, never as a plain env var. Set it with: azd env set WEBIQ_API_KEY <key>
Bing pricing tier. G2 is the tier this project has run on; G1 is the lower tier.

The curated allow-list the web tool is restricted to — a HARD boundary enforced by
Bing, which is what makes an open-web tool safe for an executive assistant. Replace
these with your own sources. boostLevel is SuperBoost or Boosted.
Assistant persona / display name (e.g. "Nuru") for the bot welcome message. Purely cosmetic; does NOT select the avatar model. Empty falls back to "Avatar".
Identity tagline under the avatar name (e.g. "Your MTN Digital Assistant"). Empty uses the company-agnostic default.
Deployment profile from `scripts/set_profile.py` — one of "web", "teams-tab", "in-call". Drives which optional channels deploy. Empty keeps the pre-profile behaviour (explicit flags only).
Enable channel C ACS Call Automation media participant ("true"/"false"). When not "true" (default), no ACS resource is created and the deployment behaves exactly as today.
ACS data residency geography (NOT an Azure region), e.g. "United States", "Europe", "Africa".
"true"/"false". Serve the .NET Teams media-bot bridge without an ACS resource (sets MEETING_BOT_ENABLED). Implied by deployProfile="in-call".
PCM sample rate (Hz) the Teams media bot streams (16000).
"true"/"false". In-call avatar only answers after a wake phrase.
"true"/"false". In-call avatar sends an outgoing video tile so it is a visible participant.
"true"/"false". Provision the Windows media host + calling bot registration. Implied by deployProfile="in-call".
Entra app client id of the CALLING bot. Must differ from botAppId.
Tenant id of the calling bot app registration. Defaults to the deployment tenant when empty.
Globally-unique DNS label for the media host public IP (becomes <label>.<region>.cloudapp.azure.com).
Local administrator password for the Windows media host.
VM size for the media host. Standard_D4s_v5 (4 vCPU) is the size proven to run the Real-Time Media Platform; a 2-vCPU host had to be resized. Lowering it is a false economy.
Public URL of the bot icon shown for the in-call avatar in Teams.
Region for the Foundry account+project (defaults to location).
Name of an existing Application Insights component to reuse. Leave empty to create a new one.
Resource group of the existing Application Insights component. Defaults to the deployment RG when empty.
Voice Live binding: "agent" (default) or "model". See modules/containerApp.bicep.
Realtime model used when voiceBinding is "model".
"true"/"false" string. Developer mode exposes the settings panel and live transcript so settings can be tried live while testing. Default "false" is the production experience, with settings locked.
Web IQ base URL — the web tool in model mode. Empty uses the code default.
Comma-separated host allow-list for Web IQ results.
Web IQ API key, passed to the container app as a secret.
Deploy Grounding with Bing Custom Search (account + site allow-list + Foundry connection). Opt-in: when false nothing Bing-related is created and the agent uses AI Search alone.
The curated site allow-list. See modules/bingGrounding.bicep for the entry shape.
Enable channel C ACS Call Automation media participant ("true"/"false"). When not "true" (default), no ACS resource is created and the container behaves as today.
ACS data residency geography (NOT an Azure region), e.g. "United States", "Europe", "Africa".
"true"/"false". Serve the .NET Teams media-bot bridge (/ws/acs/audio) without an ACS resource — sets MEETING_BOT_ENABLED. Independent of enableAcs.
PCM sample rate (Hz) the media bot streams. Teams media bot uses 16000.
"true"/"false". In-call avatar only answers after a wake phrase.
"true"/"false". In-call avatar sends an outgoing video tile (visible participant).
Principal ID of the UAMI to grant AcrPull.
Cognitive Services account (kind=AIServices) name.
Foundry project name (child of the account).
Object ID of the deployer (optional). Granted Foundry User on the account so the postprovision setup scripts can call the data plane.

Deploy the agent's chat model. Agent mode only.

The chat model backs the Foundry *agent*. Model mode binds Voice Live straight
to a realtime speech-to-speech model, which Voice Live deploys and manages
itself — it never appears as a deployment here, and nothing in the backend
reads this one. Deploying it anyway ties up quota (50K TPM) for a model that is
never called.

The embedding deployment below is NOT gated: both bindings answer from the
AI Search index, and building that index needs embeddings.
Embedding model deployment (used by setup_aisearch_index.py to vectorize data/*.docx).
Search service name to link as a Foundry project connection (optional). Leave empty to skip.
Search service endpoint (https://<name>.search.windows.net/). Required when searchServiceName is set.
Search service resource ID. Required when searchServiceName is set.
Name of the project connection created for the search service.
Resource ID of a Grounding-with-Bing-Custom-Search account to link as a project connection (optional). Leave empty to skip.
Name of the Bing account — shown as the connection display name. Required when bingAccountId is set.
Name of the project connection created for the Bing account.
Deployer object ID (optional). Granted Search Service Contributor + Index Data Contributor so setup_aisearch_index.py can create the index and upload docs locally.
Name of the Grounding-with-Bing-Custom-Search account.
Bing accounts are a global resource — this is always "global" and is not the deployment region.
Pricing tier. G2 is the tier this project has run on; G1 is the lower tier.
Name of the custom search configuration (the curated site allow-list). This is what BING_CUSTOM_CONFIG_NAME points at.

The curated allow-list the web tool is restricted to. Each entry:
  domain          — full URL, e.g. https://www.example.com/newsroom
  includeSubPages — whether pages below that path are searchable
  boostLevel      — SuperBoost | Boosted (rank weighting within the allow-list)

This is a HARD allow-list enforced by Bing: nothing outside it is reachable, which
is the property that makes an open-web tool safe to give an executive assistant.
Domains to exclude even if they sit under an allowed path.
Domains always returned for a matching query.
Always https://api.bing.microsoft.com/ — the target the Foundry connection points at.
AI Search service name (in this resource group).
Foundry project SMI principalId. Granted Search Index Data Contributor + Search Service Contributor so the agents azure_ai_search tool can read the index at runtime.
Foundry/Cognitive Services account name (in this resource group).
AI Search service SMI principalId. Granted Cognitive Services OpenAI User so the search vectorizer (authIdentity=null) can call Azure OpenAI to embed queries.
Name of the Azure Communication Services resource.
Resource tags.
Data residency / geography for the ACS resource (NOT an Azure region). e.g. "United States", "Europe", "Africa".
Name of the ACS resource (in this resource group).
Principal id of the Container App user-assigned managed identity.
Voice Live binding: "agent" routes through the Foundry agent (default, unchanged behaviour); "model" binds Voice Live straight to a realtime model with in-process tools.
Realtime model deployed by Voice Live when voiceBinding is "model". Voice Live manages this model itself — no model deployment or quota is needed.
Web IQ base URL used as the web tool in model mode. Empty falls back to the code default — the tool is gated on webIqApiKey, not on this.
Comma-separated host allow-list applied to Web IQ results. Same security boundary as bingAllowedDomains: it is what makes an open-web tool safe to hand an executive assistant.
Web IQ API key. Passed as a container-app SECRET, never as a plain env var. Empty leaves the web tool switched off.
Search service endpoint (https://<name>.search.windows.net/)
Assistant persona / display name (e.g. "Nuru") for the bot welcome message. Purely cosmetic; does NOT select the avatar model. Empty falls back to "Avatar".
Identity tagline under the avatar name (e.g. "Your MTN Digital Assistant"). Empty uses the company-agnostic default.
"true"/"false" string — frontend treats prebuilt as photo avatar when "true".
"true"/"false" string — frontend treats avatar as custom when "true".
Speech recognition model. Defaults to mai-transcribe-1; cascaded options include azure-speech, gpt-4o-transcribe.
Recognition language locale (BCP-47, e.g. en-ZA). Use "auto" to let the SR model auto-detect.
ACS endpoint for the Call Automation media participant. Empty disables channel C in the container.
"true"/"false" string. When "true", the .NET Teams media bot bridge (/ws/acs/audio) is served WITHOUT an ACS resource — sets MEETING_BOT_ENABLED so ACS_ENABLED is true on the Voice Live path alone.
PCM sample rate (Hz) the media bot streams. Teams media bot uses 16000; ACS browser bridge uses 24000.
"true"/"false" string. When "true", the in-call avatar only answers after a wake phrase so she never talks over humans.
"true"/"false" string. When "true", the in-call avatar sends an outgoing video tile so it is a visible participant instead of a faceless audio leg.

"true"/"false" string. When "true" the browser exposes the settings panel, live transcript and per-event logging, so settings can be changed and tried live while testing. Production default "false" hides the panel, locks settings and auto-starts an avatar-only experience.
Placeholder image used on first provision; azd replaces it during `azd deploy`.

metadata.description: Location for the Windows host and networking.
Entra app client id (Microsoft App ID) of the calling bot.
Tenant id of the single-tenant calling bot app registration.
The avatar brand/display name (sourced from AVATAR_DISPLAY_NAME). Becomes the meeting roster name via the Azure Bot resource. Never hardcode the custom avatar name.
Display name for the Azure Bot resource. Defaults to the avatar name so the meeting roster shows the avatar brand.
Public URL of the bot icon (the avatar logo). Shown for the bot in Teams. Leave empty to use the default Bot Framework icon.
Local administrator username for the Windows VM.
Local administrator password for the Windows VM.

VM size. Standard_D4s_v5 (4 vCPU) is the smallest size the Teams Real-Time Media Platform runs reliably on — a 2-vCPU host was tried and had to be resized. Do not lower this without re-testing a live meeting.
Globally-unique DNS label for the public IP (becomes <label>.<region>.cloudapp.azure.com).
HTTPS signaling/webhook port (Bot Framework calling notifications).
Media platform public TCP port (Real-Time Media Platform).
Resource tags.
